name: 420Registry
purpose: Canonical discovery, version history and compatibility commitments for 420 Integrated Genesis services.
invariants: REG-INV-001: A service identifier is canonical only if it is in the frozen Genesis catalog or explicitly approved as an extension.
REG-INV-002: Service versions advance exactly by one and prior version records remain readable.
REG-INV-003: Genesis-grade registration rejects implementations with no deployed runtime code.
REG-INV-004: Genesis-grade registration records the implementation runtime code hash rather than trusting a caller-supplied hash.
REG-INV-005: Every Genesis-grade registration commits a nonzero manifest hash and interface hash.
REG-INV-006: Component type, manifest, dependency root and interface commitment are immutable for a published version.
REG-INV-007: Only GovernanceTimelock may approve extension IDs, publish versions or deprecate a current version.
REG-INV-008: Deprecation fails closed for active discovery while preserving historical records.
REG-INV-009: Registry publication never grants custody, token transfer, smart-account execution, governance, bridge or validator authority to a registered implementation.
REG-INV-010: Indexers, explorers and frontends are non-canonical projections and can reconstruct registry state from chain events and reads.
REG-INV-011: Registry metadata cannot overwrite canonical state owned by Identity, Names, Rights, Pay, Bridge, Civic or other domain protocols.
REG-INV-012: Extension approval cannot alter the stable identity of any canonical Genesis service ID.
